title: Young people combine economic insecurity with purpose-driven work, local trust, early AI adoption, and renewed civic ambition
source_unit: World Economic Forum, Youth Pulse 2026: Insights From the Next Generation for a Changing World
geography: Young people aged 18-30 in 144 countries and territories, with nearly 4,600 participants from 489 locations

observations.period: 2026; youth economic outlook and personal stress

denominator.unit: approximately young people aged 18-30 surveyed across 144 countries and territories

inequality_future_trend.unit: percent selecting growing inequality between rich and poor among economic trends shaping the future

cost_housing_future_trend.unit: percent selecting increasing cost of living and housing

financial_stress.unit: percent selecting financial concerns as a major source of stress or anxiety

entrepreneurship_future_trend.unit: percent selecting the rise of entrepreneurship among economic trends shaping the future

observations.method: WEF Youth Pulse survey asking respondents to select up to three economic trends and sources of stress; the report combines quantitative responses with qualitative reflections and youth-led examples.
observations.uncertainty: The global sample is a WEF youth-perspectives survey rather than a probability sample of all young people; response composition, location coverage, and question framing limit population inference.
observations.subgroup: Young people ages 18-30 across global regions, with regional comparisons for economic outlook and entrepreneurship.
observations.counterinterpretation: Entrepreneurship and side-income activity can express agency and innovation, but may also reflect constrained access to stable jobs, capital, housing, or social protection.

observations.period: 2026; youth work, purpose, and career priorities

purpose_career_priority.unit: percent selecting a sense of purpose or meaning among future-career priorities

flexibility_balance_priority.unit: percent selecting flexibility and work-life balance

security_priority.unit: percent selecting job and financial security

youth_employment_policy_priority.unit: percent identifying youth employment and meaningful economic opportunity as a top policy priority

observations.method: WEF survey question asking respondents to select up to three career priorities and policy priorities, interpreted alongside the report's qualitative youth perspectives.
observations.uncertainty: Stated priorities do not establish job choices, labor-market outcomes, willingness to trade pay for purpose, or whether employers can deliver flexibility and meaning.
observations.subgroup: Young professionals and young adults considering work, education, purpose, flexibility, security, and policy opportunity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Purpose and balance may be aspirations shaped by insecurity rather than a rejection of pay or benefits; priorities can vary with age, region, household resources, and labor-market conditions.

observations.period: 2026; youth political trust, geopolitical concern, and participation

geopolitical_tension_future_trend.unit: percent selecting increased geopolitical tension among political trends shaping the next five years

community_leader_effectiveness.unit: percent rating community leaders very or somewhat effective in driving positive change

run_for_office_likely.unit: percent saying they are likely to run for political office

leadership_quality.value: transparency and accountability 56.4%; innovative vision and long-term thinking 54.3%

observations.method: WEF survey questions on political trends, leader effectiveness, leadership qualities, and likelihood of running for political office; response options and multi-selection rules are retained from the report.
observations.uncertainty: Perceived effectiveness and stated political ambition do not establish institutional trust, office-seeking behavior, turnout, policy influence, or successful reform; the community-leader measure is not a causal comparison.
observations.subgroup: Young people across regions, including respondents evaluating local, business, national, and media leadership.
observations.counterinterpretation: Local trust can reflect proximity and visibility rather than durable capacity; political ambition can rise alongside frustration without translating into access, representation, or institutional change.

observations.period: 2026; youth technology use, environmental concern, and consumption

ai_regular_use.unit: approximately percent reporting regular AI use to enhance skills

ai_entry_level_job_reduction.unit: approximately two-thirds believing AI will reduce entry-level job opportunities

purpose_built_communities.unit: percent saying intentionally designed youth communities provide a critical space for learning, growth, and dialogue

ethical_environmental_purchase_factors.value: environmental and ethical considerations rank among the top three factors guiding youth purchasing decisions after quality and affordability

observations.method: WEF survey and qualitative synthesis across technological, social, and environmental outlooks, including AI-use, community, and youth-consumption questions.
observations.uncertainty: Reported AI use is self-described and does not measure intensity, skill gains, job displacement, or product purchases; the community and consumption findings are not causal or representative estimates of all youth.
observations.subgroup: Young AI users, workers and learners, youth communities, consumers, and people concerned about climate and environmental degradation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Early adoption can coexist with demands for safeguards, skills, and equitable access; ethical purchasing priorities may be constrained by affordability and availability.

related_sources.claim: ILO youth-employment work provides complementary labor-market and informality context for the Youth Pulse priorities.
Pew national-pride research provides complementary cross-national identity and public-institution meaning context.

boundary: This record adds a youth-perspective route across inequality, affordability, purpose, work, local trust, geopolitical anxiety, AI adoption, climate-shaped consumption, and political participation. It uses the WEF report's aggregate survey and qualitative synthesis, not a probability-sample estimate of all young people, respondent-level prediction, causal labor-market or political models, verified AI effects, or proof that stated values determine behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official WEF Youth Pulse 2026 page and linked report PDF were retrieved and reviewed for sample frame, economic concerns, stress, career priorities, political trends, leader effectiveness, political ambition, AI use, community belonging, and values-driven consumption.
